articles.title: Arsenal get controversial referee for Nottingham Forest trip
articles.summary: Michael Oliver is back on Premier League duty this weekend, with the referee handed Arsenal’s trip to Nottingham Forest for his first Gunners involvement of...
articles.body:
Michael Oliver is back on Premier League duty this weekend, with the referee handed Arsenal's trip to Nottingham Forest for his first Gunners involvement of the season.

Arsenal visit the City Ground on Sunday, October 18, with kick-off at 4.30pm UK time and the game live on Sky Sports.

Michael Oliver will return to Premier League action this weekend for Arsenal 's trip to Nottingham Forest , his first involvement in a Gunners match this season in any capacity.

For some unexplained reason, Oliver had no Premier League appointment last weekend when the competition resumed after the international break for the first time after Manchester City 's guilty verdict.

He now returns with Arsenal, a club whose matches have featured a number of contentious decisions involving Oliver.

Against City in October 2023, Oliver booked Mateo Kovacic for a red card challenge on Martin Odegaard , then declined to show him a second yellow after another red card challenge on Declan Rice .

Howard Webb subsequently said Kovacic was "an extremely fortunate player to stay on the field of play" and that the second challenge should have brought another booking.

VAR, they said, was unable to intervene because it concerned a potential second yellow rather than a straight red, even though it should have been a straight red.

Oliver was again at the centre of controversy when Wolves faced Arsenal in January 2025.

He sent off Myles Lewis-Skelly for serious foul play, but an independent FA commission unanimously upheld Arsenal's wrongful-dismissal claim in record quick time.

After that red card, Arsenal were fined three times the normal amount for their protests.

The commission's written reasons found that Oliver "had made an obvious error" and that Lewis-Skelly had neither endangered his opponent's safety nor used excessive force.

The suspension was withdrawn, but the fine stood.

Oliver also incorrectly sent Gabriel Martinelli off after showing two yellow cards in the same passage of play, having played advantage without informing the Arsenal forward that he would be booked for the first offence. That was also against Wolves.

Because the dismissal came after two yellows, Arsenal were unable to appeal.

Photo by ADRIAN DENNIS/AFP via Getty Images

Let's also not forget the time he sent Leandro Trossard off against Manchester City for kicking the ball away, or when he booked Lewis-Skelly, at the time a sub, for passing on a message to David Raya . Funnily enough, that was also in a game against City.

Oliver's overseas refereeing work has also attracted scrutiny.

He took charge of Al-Hilal 's 2-0 victory over Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia in April 2023 , with reporting at the time saying he had PGMOL permission and received around £3,000 plus business-class travel.

Oliver also travelled to referee Sharjah against Al-Ain in the United Arab Emirates in September 2023 alongside Darren England , Dan Cook and Stuart Burt . Burt will also be involved in Arsenal's game this weekend.

The criticism arose from the perception of a conflict of interest, with English referees accepting paid work in a state-backed league in the country associated with City's ownership.

Reporting also pointed to City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak 's position on the board of the league's principal sponsor, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company .

The UAE trip also preceded the incorrect disallowing of Luis Diaz 's goal in Tottenham Hotspur 's victory over Liverpool , when England and Cook were working as VAR and assistant VAR.

Webb later said : "In terms of that specific trip out to the Middle East, there was no link found from that to the error."

Oliver's absence from last weekend's Premier League programme came as a surprise, with Chris Kavanagh taking charge of Liverpool against Manchester City.

Arsenal arrive in Nottingham having won nine of their last 10 matches in all competitions, scoring 17 goals, conceding six and keeping four clean sheets.

Forest have won just one of their seven fixtures this season, drawing two and losing four. They have scored five goals while conceding 10.

Oliver will be assisted by Burt and James Mainwaring , with Farai Hallam as fourth official. Hallam will also referee Manchester City's game on Saturday.

Michael Salisbury will be on VAR, assisted by Ian Hussin . Salisbury was 4th official for Arsenal's game against Brighton , while Mainwaring was assistant VAR for the same match.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho wants more attacking options at Real Madrid despite reaching 500-goal milestone
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho wants Real Madrid to become even more dangerous in attack, despite reaching a significant milestone during their 4-3 victory over AS Roma.Accor...
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho wants Real Madrid to become even more dangerous in attack, despite reaching a significant milestone during their 4-3 victory over AS Roma .

According to MARCA , it has come to light that Antonio Rudiger's goal against Roma helped Mourinho's Real Madrid reach 500 goals under his management.

However, the achievement has not changed the Portuguese coach's desire to add more variety to his team's attacking play.

In fact, Mourinho wants a side capable of controlling possession, launching rapid counter-attacks and creating danger from set pieces, all without losing the defensive discipline that defines his approach.

Mourinho targets attacking variety at Real Madrid

Real Madrid already have considerable firepower at their disposal, with Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Jr., Yan Diomande, Arda Guler, Carlos Espi and Endrick, giving Mourinho several attacking options.

On top of that, the injured Rodrygo would provide another high-quality alternative once available.

Hence, the challenge is not only to score more goals, but to make Real Madrid less predictable.

Real Madrid have now scored 500 goals under Jose Mourinho. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images)

Mourinho wants his forwards to exploit their pace in transition while ensuring the team can also break down opponents through patient build-up play.

Set pieces are another important part of his plans, as combining those threats with defensive organisation would give the team more ways to control matches and punish different types of opposition.

Mourinho reaches 500 goals for Real Madrid

Rudiger's strike against Roma carried added significance because it took Mourinho to 500 goals in 188 matches as Real Madrid manager.

That works out at an average of 2.66 goals per game, the best return among club managers who have overseen at least 50 matches.

La Liga accounts for the largest share, with Real Madrid scoring 345 goals in 122 matches.

They have added 92 goals in 38 Champions League games, 55 in 24 Copa del Rey matches and eight in four Spanish Super Cup fixtures.

Mourinho wants a more versatile attack for Real Madrid. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images)

Their biggest victory during this spell came in the 2010-11 Copa del Rey, when Madrid beat Levante 8-0.

This season, though, the team are averaging 2.5 goals per match.

Mourinho wants more from Real Madrid's attack

The numbers underline Real Madrid's scoring power, but Mourinho is looking beyond the milestone.

His ambition is to build a more versatile attack that can adapt to different opponents rather than rely solely on individual brilliance or quick transitions.

With Mbappe and Vinicius offering pace and penetration, and several other options providing different qualities, Madrid have the personnel to develop that flexibility.

Hence, the next step is making those strengths work together consistently.

articles.title: The 6 best college football games to watch in Week 7
articles.summary: 6 games in Week 7 that you need to look out for this weekend.
articles.body:
Last weekend was far and away the wildest of the 2026 college football season, and it's left us with another fun slate for Week 7. We're at the halfway point of the season, and the games keep getting bigger and more pivotal week by week.

This part of the season matters so much as we enter the stretch run, when everyone will be jockeying for position in their respective conferences.

Here at Sooners Wire, we're going to have our eyes all over the home SEC opener for the Oklahoma Sooners , as the Kentucky Wildcats come to Norman on Saturday night for a 6:30 p.m. kickoff. It's a very important game for both teams, even if it is overshadowed by some of the even bigger matchups this week. That's how impressive the slate for this Saturday is.

Here are the top six games to watch in Week 7.

Ohio State and Indiana look like the two best teams in the Big Ten right now, and this could preview the league's title game, a rematch from last season. These two teams are talented enough to win it all this year. The Buckeyes already have a loss on the season, but they've been rock-solid since that point. Head coach Ryan Day knows that a win on the road this week can push his team right back to the top of the pecking order in the country. Quarterback Julian Sayin will have to play mistake-free football against a very sound defense.

The Hoosiers are one of just two unbeaten teams left in the Big Ten, and they escaped with a close win on the road last week over Nebraska. Now, head coach Curt Cignetti's team comes back home to Bloomington, looking to add another win to the nation's longest winning streak. The offense, led by quarterback Josh Hoover, will have to keep up with the juggernaut on the other sideline.

Notre Dame and BYU will both enter this week undefeated, and neither team has been tested this season like they will be on Saturday. Two teams that narrowly missed the College Football Playoff last season are determined to make it this year. The Fighting Irish have breezed through a less-than-challenging schedule through the first half of their season, making short work of just about everyone they've faced. Quarterback CJ Carr runs the show on offense, and head coach Marcus Freeman has a very talented squad that will have to play well on the road this week.

The Cougars will also get a severe jump in competition this week, and Provo should be a great environment on Saturday night. A physical offense led by quarterback Bear Bachmeier will be tested at home, and head coach Kalani Sitake's team hopes to take the next step with a huge statement win in a highlight game.

Missouri and Ole Miss are right in the thick of things in the SEC standings , and each team has just one loss entering Week 7. This game can catapult one school toward contention in the conference. The Tigers are red-hot, having knocked off Florida and Texas A&M in dominant fashion in consecutive weeks. Now, a road test awaits head coach Eliah Drinkwitz and the Tigers. Quarterback Austin Simmons will face his former school this week, after he was replaced as the signal-caller last year by Lane Kiffin in favor of Trinidad Chambliss. He's been excellent through the first month and a half of the season.

The Rebels were stunned on the road against Florida a few weeks ago, and they've been a bit out of the spotlight since. However, they're still very much a threat in the SEC, especially with their high-powered offense. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who took the starting job from Simmons early last season, leads the way, and this game could turn into a shootout. Head coach Pete Golding hopes to lean on what should be a great crowd in Oxford.

Alabama and Tennessee will meet in the "Third Saturday in October" rivalry matchup. It's another big-time matchup featuring a pair of one-loss SEC schools. The teams have split the last four meetings, which have produced some epic moments in recent years. The Crimson Tide lost a very close game last week against Georgia, and they'll look to take out some of that frustration in this game. Head coach Kalen DeBoer has a very good team, and a big road win would put them right back in the hunt. Quarterback Keelon Russell has been a star this season, and he'll have to play well against a good defense led by defensive coordinator Jim Knowles.

The Volunteers have two close wins in the last two weeks, but they'll need to play better this week to pull off the upset. Head coach Josh Heupel faces a decision on his starting quarterback. Both Faizon Brandon and George MacIntyre have had their good moments this year, but the offense needs one of them to step up, stay healthy, and make the job theirs. They have a great opportunity to do that this week at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville.

5. Mississippi State at LSU, 11:00 a.m. CT

This could turn into a CFP elimination game for Mississippi State and LSU, as both teams took it on the chin in their most recent games. For the Bulldogs, a disappointing loss to Alabama two weeks ago marked their first loss of the season. Head coach Jeff Lebby has found success with speed on the outside and the play of their quarterback, but Kamario Taylor's status is up in the air ahead of their showdown in Baton Rouge. Parker Puckett could be under center against LSU this week.

The Tigers lost on the road to Kentucky, and they'll return to Death Valley with two losses and their backs against the wall. Head coach Lane Kiffin and his team entered the year with high expectations, but they could come crashing down with another loss this week. Quarterback Sam Leavitt will look to keep that from happening in Tiger Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

6. Oklahoma State at Houston, 6:30 p.m. CT

Oklahoma State and Houston are trying to see where they stack up in the Big 12 at this point in the season, and this game will be a good measuring stick for both teams in a wide-open league. The Cowboys have won four straight games, as many as they did in the 2024 and 2025 seasons combined. New head coach Eric Morris has been successful so far, and his team scores in bunches. Quarterback Drew Mestemaker runs the show and is receiving buzz as the top quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft.

The Cougars have won three straight games, and they've had an impressive season ahead of this week's test. Head coach Willie Fritz will need a strong defensive performance to win at home, and he'll need his offense to keep pace if it turns into a high-scoring affair. At the controls on that side of the ball is quarterback Conner Weigman, who has been great for the Cougars after transferring over from Texas A&M. It's a crucial game in the Big 12 for both schools.

articles.title: Alex Scott transfer news: Bournemouth will consider offers in excess of £80m for England international amid refusal to sign new contract
articles.summary: Chelsea and Liverpool retain a serious interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott; Manchester City, Arsenal, Manchester United and Tottenham were interested before they strengthened their midfield with other options in the summer; Scott made his full England debut earlier this month
articles.body:
If a big offer came in for him in January, it is something the club would have to consider. While Scott will not agitate for a move, he is ambitious and keen on exploring his options with bigger clubs.

Chelsea and Liverpool retain a serious interest in the 23-year-old, as did Manchester City, Arsenal, Manchester United and Tottenham before they strengthened their midfield with other options in the summer, after being told by Bournemouth Scott was not for sale.

Scott's existing contract expires in just over 18 months, and Bournemouth are aware that his value will only shrink further as time passes.

While they do not want to sell him, we have been told they may be open to offers for him in January if the club is practically safe from relegation. Bournemouth have yet to win a Premier League game so far this season, and lost 5-1 at Chelsea last weekend.

Sources have suggested to Sky Sports News an offer in excess of £80m with add-ons would have to be taken seriously by Bournemouth in January.

Scott faces many more weeks on the treatment table after exacerbating a thigh tendon injury whilst away with England, when he made his full senior debut.

Rose: Scott still committed to Bournemouth

Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose has insisted Scott is committed to the club despite talk growing about a January exit.

Asked about Scott's future on Wednesday ahead of Bournemouth's Europa League game with Sturm Graz, Rose said: "We just closed the other transfer window and we're now talking about the next one.

"We are just focused on the game [against Sturm Graz] and the upcoming game in the Premier League - and not commentating on rumours that show up right after the last transfer window closes.

"It's not frustrating anyway for us. I told you that Alex Scott was going to stay in the summer. We got questions after questions in press conferences for I don't know how many weeks.

"He's a player of our club and now he's injured, we are looking forward to having him back in a couple of days and weeks and we'll continue with Alex Scott.

"And he's quite committed, everyone can see it from the first games [of the season]."
